Subject: DPA redline - aggregated telemetry carveout

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking a look. Attached is our marked-up DPA focusing on a narrow carveout: TideHealth needs explicit permission to collect aggregated, non-identifiable model telemetry and billing counters (e.g., model_id, token_count_by_request_type, latency percentiles, feature-flagged event counts) to support billing reconciliation and product quality metrics.

Our legal team is requesting: 1) a short exhibit that permits collection of aggregated telemetry used for billing and product improvement, 2) express allowance for a single analytics subprocessor (Quantlytics Inc.) that will only receive pre-aggregated metrics, and 3) a 90-day retention window for aggregated metrics.

We attached our redline (TideHealth_DPA_redline_v3.docx) and a proposed metrics schema (metrics_schema.csv). Can Redwood confirm whether this language is acceptable, and whether Product/Security will need any implementation caveats? Also, please confirm Quantlytics as an allowed subprocessor and provide SOC2 / contractual evidence.

We'd like to close this by next Wednesday (2026-12-23) if possible.

Best,
Ana Sanchez
Head of Procurement, TideHealth

Irene / Priya,

High level: I'm okay in principle with a narrow aggregated-metrics carveout but we need hard controls. Specific asks from Security: 
- Retention: reduce to 30 days for aggregated telemetry unless Tide provides a business justification tied to billing reconciliation (we can consider 90 days for explicit billing counters only).
- Pseudonymization: no persistent customer identifiers in metrics. If you must use an ID for dedup, it must be a salted hash under our KMS for 48 hours only.
- Subprocessor: Quantlytics must provide SOC 2 Type II (relevant to security & availability) and sign our subprocessor contract addendum limiting data to pre-aggregated metrics; no raw logs.
- Access controls: RBAC proof, audit logs, and attestation of no cross-tenant joins.
- Encryption: in-transit + at-rest with customer-managed KMS (preferred) or customer-shared KMS; if not possible, limit retention to 14 days.

Suggested redline text (short):
"Redwood and Customer may exchange non-identifiable, aggregated telemetry and billing counters for the purposes of billing reconciliation and product quality improvement. Such telemetry shall not contain direct identifiers or raw request payloads; any ephemeral identifiers used for deduplication must be pseudonymized and deleted within 48 hours. Any subprocessor receiving such telemetry must: (a) be listed in Schedule X; (b) provide SOC2 Type II evidence relevant to the processing; and (c) be bound by contract to process only pre-aggregated metrics. Retention for product telemetry is limited to 30 days unless parties agree in writing to a subset retained for billing reconciliation up to 90 days."

I'll need Quantlytics SOC2 and a signed subprocessor addendum before I can sign off.

-Olga
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Irene / Olga,

Product notes: we can deliver the requested aggregated metrics but there are a few implementation caveats to call out so Tide is not surprised: 
- Schema: metrics_schema.csv looks fine for counts/latencies. We'll need to add two fields (sample_rate, hashed_customer_token) and a flag to indicate "billing_counter" vs "product_metric".
- Sampling: some high-volume events will be sampled; sampled metrics will be annotated. That could create small divergence vs raw billing logs (we should call it out in the carveout).
- Opt-out: customers should be able to opt out of product telemetry (we already support this), but opting out may impact product improvement features.
- Timeline: engineering estimates 3 weeks to add fields and 1 week for testing; deployment in Canary then Prod (2 weeks total) — so ~6 weeks from signoff for full pipeline.

Proposed language (product-friendly, short):
"Redwood may emit and share pre-aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry and billing counters as set forth in Exhibit Y. Where metrics are sampled, Redwood will annotate sampling rates and provide an error margin estimate. Customers may opt out of product telemetry; opting out may limit product improvement analytics and certain derived, non-personal features"

I agree with Olga on retention and subprocessor evidence. For hashed ids we can implement an ephemeral salt and ensure storage is ephemeral. Happy to help draft the consolidated paragraph and include the sampling caveat.

- Priya
Director, Product Management, Redwood Inference

Hi Ana (and Tide team),

Thanks for the redline and schema. We discussed internally with Product and Security and can provisionally accept a narrow carveout with these conditions: 

1) Scope & content: Redwood will share only pre-aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry and billing counters as outlined in the attached metrics_schema.csv (we propose adding 'sample_rate' and 'hashed_customer_token' fields). Sampling will be annotated and documented.

2) Retention: Product telemetry retention is limited to 30 days. For explicit billing counters used for reconciliation (and listed in Exhibit Y) retention may be extended to 90 days upon written agreement and business justification.

3) Subprocessor: Quantlytics Inc. is acceptable only after Tide provides Quantlytics' SOC2 Type II report and Quantlytics signs Redwood's subprocessor addendum limiting processing to pre-aggregated metrics. Please provide SOC2 evidence and point of contact for Quantlytics legal.

4) Pseudonymization & access: Any ephemeral identifier used for deduplication must be pseudonymized (salted hash) and auto-deleted within 48 hours. Access to aggregated metrics must be controlled via RBAC and logged.

5) Implementation caveats: Metrics that are sampled will include sampling rate and an estimated error margin; opting out of product telemetry is available but will affect product analytics. Engineering expects ~6 weeks to deliver pipeline changes to support the agreed schema and annotations.

We are prepared to incorporate the language above into the DPA exhibit. Pending receipt of Quantlytics SOC2 and a signed subprocessor addendum, Security will sign off. Please confirm acceptance of these conditions or propose alternative language.

Best regards,
Irene Choi
Director, Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
